sources.shortSummary: Notebook session sharing is configured in workspace Spark settings and requires a matching user, workspace, default lakehouse, compute configuration, and packages.
sources.title: Configure high concurrency mode for Fabric notebooks

sources.shortSummary: Git synchronization versions supported item definitions. Feature branches/workspaces and reviewed integration complement deployment-pipeline stage promotion. Questions use established Git and deployment behavior, not planned capabilities mentioned elsewhere on the page.
sources.title: Fabric CI/CD concepts and best practices

sources.shortSummary: Warehouse connectivity uses Fabric permissions while SQL permissions provide object-level granularity. Row and column security restrict data access; audit activities record user actions.
sources.title: Secure your Fabric Data Warehouse

sources.shortSummary: Dynamic masking alters nonprivileged query results without changing stored values. UNMASK and CONTROL can expose originals. Masking alone does not prevent inference through arbitrary queries.
sources.title: Dynamic data masking in Fabric Data Warehouse

sources.shortSummary: Pipeline parameters enable reuse. Direct expressions can preserve numeric types; string interpolation returns text. The distinction matters for typed activity properties.
sources.title: Parameters for Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric

sources.shortSummary: Fabric supports PySpark in interactive notebooks and Spark batch jobs, with session or environment library management. This grounds use of standard Spark DataFrame APIs in Fabric.
sources.title: Use Python for Apache Spark

sources.shortSummary: Activator can respond to Fabric job events with Teams/email notifications or follow-up activities. Scheduled-failure emails have a simpler monitoring-hub option; blind retries do not fix deterministic errors.
sources.title: Respond to Fabric events with Activator

sources.shortSummary: An incremental copy uses old/new watermark lookups, an exclusive-lower/inclusive-upper interval, and success-dependent watermark persistence. The source column must track relevant changes.
sources.title: Incrementally load data from Data Warehouse to Lakehouse

sources.shortSummary: Shortcuts reference existing data without moving it. Delta targets can be exposed as tables; actual copying is needed when approved regional placement requires physical relocation.
sources.title: Shortcuts in a lakehouse

sources.shortSummary: Standard PySpark DataFrame grouping and aggregation syntax, paired with Fabric's Python-support source. Databricks-specific workspace or catalog behavior is outside the questions.
sources.title: PySpark basics

sources.shortSummary: KQL arg_max returns columns from a row maximizing an expression, unlike scalar max. A by clause selects a maximizing row independently per group.
sources.title: arg_max() (aggregation function)

sources.shortSummary: Reduce KQL data volume early, prioritize selective datetime filtering, and use token-aware has when token semantics are required. Keep optimizations semantically equivalent.
sources.title: Best practices for Kusto Query Language queries

sources.shortSummary: Eventstream SQL supports tumbling and hopping windows. Arrival time is the default; event-time processing requires TIMESTAMP BY. Questions test documented window behavior.
sources.title: Process events by using a SQL operator

sources.shortSummary: Spark streaming watermarks, bounded deduplication, and temporal join conditions control retained state. The questions exclude experimental state readers and new-runtime custom-state APIs mentioned on this page.
sources.title: Stateful processing with Structured Streaming

sources.shortSummary: Eventhouse system overview separates ingestion counts, query activity, storage, and schema changes. The Ingestion tile shows ingested rows and receiving databases.
sources.title: Manage and monitor an eventhouse

sources.shortSummary: Monitoring hub activity details and historical runs support status, duration, error, and refresh investigations. Contributors can configure scheduled-failure email notifications.
sources.title: Use the Microsoft Fabric monitoring hub

sources.shortSummary: Pipeline monitoring exposes per-activity input/output and performance duration breakdowns, enabling evidence-based diagnosis rather than speculative tuning.
sources.title: Monitor pipeline runs in Fabric Data Factory

sources.shortSummary: Pipeline property-type errors require correcting the provided value type. Used with parameter and monitoring documentation to diagnose string interpolation at a numeric property.
sources.title: Troubleshoot pipelines for Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric

sources.shortSummary: Exit code 137 and skewed stage input can indicate executor memory pressure. Stage evidence guides partition, skew-handling, and memory remedies rather than merely increasing failure tolerance.
sources.title: Troubleshoot Spark memory and performance issues

sources.shortSummary: Shortcut access depends on identity and permissions along the read path. T-SQL Delegated identity mode is an explicit exception using the item owner's target access before consumer OneLake-role filtering.
sources.title: OneLake shortcut security

sources.shortSummary: Named-field identity ingestion mapping is case-sensitive. Misaligned JSON names or types can produce empty or incorrect columns; explicit mappings can align source fields to table columns.
sources.title: Ingestion mappings

sources.shortSummary: Local Delta maintenance distinguishes OPTIMIZE compaction from VACUUM retention cleanup. Short retention can affect history and concurrent workloads. The separate preview pipeline maintenance activity is not tested.
sources.title: Run Delta table maintenance in lakehouse

sources.shortSummary: Warehouse cold starts can include compute initialization, remote reads, and statistics work. Repeated comparable runs and remote-storage scan history help avoid misleading benchmark conclusions.
sources.title: Performance guidelines in Fabric Data Warehouse
